about.title: Hesperia Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A fall rarely feels like a legal matter in the moment. You are on the ground in a store aisle off Bear Valley Road or in a dim parking lot along Main Street, and your first thought is whether anything is broken. In California, though, the property owner's responsibility comes down to one question: did they know, or should they have known, about the hazard and fail to fix it or warn you? That is called notice, and it is the heart of a Hesperia premises liability claim. Owners across San Bernardino County are held to this standard whether the property is a big-box store, an apartment complex, or a private home. Proving notice depends on evidence that fades fast. Surveillance footage gets overwritten, spills get mopped, and cracked walkways get patched. We handle Hesperia premises liability claims on a contingency basis, so you can focus on healing while our team focuses on preserving what actually happened.

whyChoose.title: Why Hesperia Fall Victims Choose Us

items.title: Notice is the whole case
items.desc: California does not hold owners liable simply because you fell on their property. Our team knows how to gather cleaning logs, prior complaints, and inspection records that show the owner knew or should have known about the hazard.

items.title: Video and photos vanish quickly
items.desc: Most stores and complexes along Main Street and Bear Valley Road keep camera footage for only a short window. We can send a preservation demand early so the recording of your fall is not simply overwritten.

items.title: Partial fault does not end your claim
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so even if you were texting or wearing worn shoes, you may still recover a reduced share. That is very different from being told you have no case.

items.question: I fell at a shopping center in Hesperia but did not report it that day. Is it too late?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Reporting late can make notice harder to prove, but it does not automatically defeat a claim. Write down everything you remember now, photograph the spot if it still exists, and note anyone who saw you fall. We can evaluate what evidence remains and whether the property owner still has video.

items.question: What if I tripped on a sidewalk or at a park owned by the City of Hesperia or San Bernardino County?
items.answer: Claims against public entities in California follow a much shorter timeline than the standard two years, and they usually require a formal government claim first. Missing that early step can close the door entirely. Because of that, falls on public property deserve a quick conversation with us rather than a wait-and-see approach.

items.question: Do you charge anything to review my case?
items.answer: No. Our initial case review is free. We handle premises liability cases on contingency, meaning there is no attorney fee unless money is recovered for you. You can ask us directly about our fee structure before agreeing to anything.
